title: Dirty Frag Defensive Threat Model
scope: Post-compromise Linux local privilege-escalation risk involving exposed esp4, esp6, or rxrpc kernel module paths, modeled for defensive architecture review and executive presentation.
safety_boundary: Defensive visualization only; excludes exploit mechanics, payload guidance, kernel corruption primitives, and step-by-step weaponization.

trust_zones.label: External / attacker-controlled context
trust_zones.description: Internet-originated access, compromised credentials, web shell operators, or other untrusted sources before local code execution.

trust_zones.label: Compromised low-privileged Linux context
trust_zones.description: A user, service account, web process, or container workload where an adversary already has local execution but not root.

trust_zones.label: Kernel and module attack surface
trust_zones.description: Host kernel, module loading policy, and Dirty Frag-relevant esp4, esp6, and rxrpc exposure conditions.

trust_zones.label: Privileged host and business assets
trust_zones.description: Root context, credentials, application data, GLPI/PHP session stores, secrets, and lateral-movement opportunities.

trust_zones.label: Defender controls and telemetry
trust_zones.description: Patch management, module policy, EDR/SIEM telemetry, osquery, detections, incident response, and exception governance.

components.label: Initial foothold source
components.summary: Phished SSH credential, exposed web application, web shell, compromised container workload, or similar post-compromise entry point.

components.label: Low-privileged execution
components.summary: Interactive shell, service process, PHP runtime, or workload identity able to execute local commands.

components.label: Local staging paths
components.summary: Writable temporary directories or application paths used for suspicious tooling, logs, or session artifacts.

components.label: esp4 / esp6 / rxrpc exposure
components.summary: Dirty Frag-relevant modules loaded, loadable, or insufficiently governed by modprobe policy.

components.label: User-to-kernel privilege boundary
components.summary: Boundary where post-compromise local execution can become root impact if vulnerability and prerequisites are present.

components.label: Root context
components.summary: Administrative control of the host with ability to change files, credentials, security tooling, and workloads.

components.label: Credentials, sessions, and data
components.summary: GLPI/PHP session data, service secrets, configuration, logs, and business data exposed after privilege escalation.

components.label: Patch and module controls
components.summary: Kernel patching, reboot compliance, module deny rules, container hardening, least privilege, and shell access governance.

components.label: Telemetry and hunting controls
components.summary: KQL, Sigma, osquery, EDR, module-load telemetry, root-transition monitoring, and suspicious file/session activity hunts.

components.label: IR and exception governance
components.summary: Forensic triage, containment, rebuild decisions, exception approvals, risk acceptance, and executive reporting.

threats.description: Use of stolen credentials or service identities to obtain the local foothold required before Dirty Frag matters.
Modification of session files, web application state, security tooling, logs, or configuration after root access.
Log gaps or weak process lineage that make root-transition timelines difficult to prove.
Exposure of credentials, secrets, GLPI/PHP session data, kernel posture, or sensitive business data.
Operational disruption from kernel instability, containment actions, emergency reboots, or incompatible module mitigations.
A low-privileged local actor can become root if affected kernel paths and exploit preconditions align.

controls.label: Disable or deny unused esp4, esp6, and rxrpc modules after dependency review
Reduce unnecessary SSH, shell, sudo, and container escape blast radius
Deploy Dirty Frag KQL, Sigma, and osquery hunts from this repository
Alert on unexpected module load, unload, and inspection activity
Investigate suspicious GLPI/PHP session modification patterns
Preserve evidence, contain suspected hosts, rotate secrets, and rebuild when integrity is uncertain
